title: The domain map: from semantic engineering to the stages of the flow

sections.name: summary
sections.label: In short
sections.content: Where our work happens, from the base domain down to the stages of the flow. A domain says where and when a problem occurs; its tensions say what it trades off.

sections.name: tree
sections.label: The map
sections.content:
Semantic engineering in practice is the base domain. Within it:
- Programme coordination: how work and decisions move through the programme. It is refined by the nine stages of the archetypal flow, each a domain with its own purpose, scope and trade-off: Sense, Make meaning, Choose a response, Shape the work, Allocate, Build, Review and land, Decide, Learn and remember.
- Semantic records: what a record is and asserts.
- Agent memory: what agents keep between sessions.
- Deep context: the context an agent needs to act well.
- Evidence-backed writing: writing whose claims carry their evidence.
- Group meaning ownership: how a group owns its meaning.
- Stance: the position a record or response takes.

sections.name: drill
sections.label: How to read it
sections.content: Open a domain to see its purpose and scope, then its clusters, problems, tensions and poles. Open a stage under Programme coordination to see its exercise (what we tried and where we went too far), its trade-off and the two poles. Most domains exist as a suggestion and an affirmed copy; the map shows the record each domain's own section is built on.

sections.name: state
sections.label: Where it stands
sections.content: The nine stages and Programme coordination came from the flow work (2026-10-25). Choose a response and Shape the work have no affirmed copy yet. The tensions are untested.
